issue.title: [Architecture] Discovery Query Diversification & Repository Concentration Monopoly
issue.body:
## 1. Problem Description: Why Discovery Shows Few Repos and Low Match Scores (36% - 42%)

### Observation
In user testing of Discovery:
1. **Single Repository Domination:** 4 out of 6 displayed issues belong to a single repository (`dolev31/lasagna`).
2. **Low Relevance Scores:** Match scores hover between **36% and 42%**, rarely exceeding 50%.
3. **Limited Repository Diversity:** Users see issues from only 1 or 2 distinct organizations rather than a broad cross-section of open-source projects.

---

## 2. Root Cause Breakdown

### A. Why One Repository Dominates
GitHub's Search API evaluates queries globally and orders them by `sort:updated-desc`.
If a maintainer at `dolev31/lasagna` triages 10 issues simultaneously or a bot touches multiple tickets, all 10 tickets get identical, recent `updated_at` timestamps.
Because Scout's discovery query:
```
is:open is:issue label:"help wanted" language:Python sort:updated-desc
```
fetches the first 50 results in a single bulk request without repository deduplication, that single active repository floods 80% of the returned list!

### B. Why Match Scores are Capped at 36% - 42%
In `apps/web/src/utils/relevanceScorer.ts`, the 100-point deterministic formula is structured as follows:
- **Language Match:** 35 points (Matches user's primary language `Python` or `TypeScript`).
- **Tech / Framework Match:** 25 points (Matches user's specific frameworks like `FastAPI`, `React`, `Django`).
- **Recency:** 15 points (~5 to 8 points for issues older than 7 days).
- **Competition:** 15 points (0 points if already commented or high stars).
- **Difficulty:** 10 points.

**The Math:**
- If an issue is written in `Python`, it gets `+35 pts`.
- But if the repository's GitHub topics do NOT explicitly include the user's specific favorite frameworks (e.g. `FastAPI`, `Pandas`), **Tech Score = 0 / 25**.
- Recency contributes `~5 pts`.
- Total Score: **35 + 0 + 5 = 40% (36% - 42%)**!
Without analyzing the issue body or expanding topic synonyms, the scoring engine plateaus at ~40%.

---

## 3. Architectural Solution

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User Profile: Skills, Frameworks, Languages] --> B[Multi-Query Generator]
    B --> C1[Query 1: Lang=Python + Framework Topics]
    B --> C2[Query 2: Lang=TypeScript + Good First Issue]
    B --> C3[Query 3: Curated High-Signal Repos]
    
    C1 --> D[GitHub Search Multi-Fetch]
    C2 --> D
    C3 --> D
    
    D --> E[Repository Diversity Limiter: Max 2 Issues Per Repo]
    E --> F[Body Text NLP / Topic Synonym Expansion]
    F --> G[Elevated Relevance Scores: 70% - 95%]
    G --> H[Diverse, High-Signal Discovery Feed]
```

### 1. Repository Diversity Capping (Max 2 Per Repo)
In `useIssueDiscovery.ts`, enforce a repository diversification pass:
```typescript
const repoCounts = new Map<string, number>();
const diverseIssues = scoredIssues.filter(issue => {
  const count = repoCounts.get(issue.repo) || 0;
  if (count >= 2) return false; // Cap at 2 issues per repo in Top 20
  repoCounts.set(issue.repo, count + 1);
  return true;
});
```

### 2. Multi-Query Skill Interleaving
Instead of one monolithic search query, execute 2 parallel queries:
- Query A: Primary language with `good first issue` or `help wanted`.
- Query B: User's top framework keyword (e.g. `fastapi`, `nextjs`, `tailwind`).
- Interleave and deduplicate results to ensure broad representation across different projects.

### 3. Issue Body Keyword Scanning
Enhance `relevanceScorer.ts` to scan the issue title and first 500 characters of the issue body for user framework keywords, awarding partial credit (up to 15/25 pts) even when GitHub repository topics are missing.

---

## 4. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No single repository occupies more than 2 slots in the top 10 Discovery results.
- [ ] Framework matching scans issue titles and body snippets in addition to repository topics.
- [ ] Discovery surfaces diverse issues matching user preferences with high-signal scores (>70%).

issue.title: [Bug / UX] Discovery cards display confusing 'UNEVALUATED' badge despite showing Mathematical Match Score
issue.body:
## 1. Problem & Root Cause

### The Bug / UX Confusion
In Mission Control under the **Discovery** tab:
1. Every card prominently displays a match score (e.g. `42% Match` or `36% Match`).
2. Directly beside it, a status tag reads: `UNEVALUATED` in gray text.

### Root Cause Analysis in `apps/web/src/components/IssueCard.tsx`
```tsx
// apps/web/src/components/IssueCard.tsx:43-52
let scoreLabel = 'UNEVALUATED';
let scoreColor = 'text-gray-400 bg-gray-500/10 border-gray-500/20';

if (issue.difficultyScore !== undefined && issue.difficultyScore !== null) {
  if (issue.difficultyScore <= 3) {
    scoreLabel = 'BEGINNER FRIENDLY';
    ...
  }
}
```
- The card relies on `issue.difficultyScore` (which is only populated when an issue passes through full AI evaluation).
- Because Discovery intentionally avoids running expensive AI calls on 50 raw search results to conserve LLM quotas, `issue.difficultyScore` is `null`.
- Consequently, the UI marks every single issue as `UNEVALUATED`.
- **User Impact:** Users interpret `UNEVALUATED` as meaning the system failed to evaluate their skills, leading them to believe that the `42% Match` is either broken, arbitrary, or uncomputed.

---

## 2. Proposed UI/UX Solution

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [⚡ 42% Match (Skills & Language)]       [✨ AI Evaluate Difficulty] |
|                                                                       |
|  Import/export json-schemas and OpenAPI schemas                       |
|  unionai-oss/pandera                                                  |
|  [enhancement] [help wanted] [python]                                 |
|                                                                       |
|  [ View Issue ↗ ]    [ 🚀 Claim This Issue ]              [ 🔖 Save ] |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Decouple Heuristic Match from AI Evaluation:**
   - Instead of displaying a confusing `UNEVALUATED` badge, label the match source clearly:
     - `Heuristic Match: 42%` (with an info tooltip explaining: *"Scored via deterministic language & framework overlap"*).
2. **On-Demand AI Evaluation Action:**
   - Add a lightweight button on each card: `[✨ AI Quick Check]`.
   - Clicking this runs a single on-demand LLM evaluation for that specific card, updating the badge to:
     - `🟢 AI Verified: High Fit (Beginner Friendly)`
     - `🟡 AI Verified: Moderate Complexity`
3. **Transparent Evaluation Status:**
   - Display a persistent hint: *"Skills matched deterministically. Click 'Claim' or 'AI Quick Check' to generate deep architecture analysis."*

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Remove the misleading `UNEVALUATED` badge when a heuristic relevance score is present.
- [ ] Clearly label the deterministic score as `Heuristic Match: XX%`.
- [ ] Add an on-demand `[✨ AI Evaluate]` trigger to evaluate individual cards without burning batch quota.

issue.title: [Architecture] AI Evaluation Rate-Limiting Strategy: Multi-Tier Quotas (RPM/RPD) and Lazy vs Speculative Evaluation
issue.body:
## 1. Architectural Problem: AI Rate Limits vs Full Issue Discovery

### The Challenge
When a user opens Discovery, the system fetches up to **50 candidate issues**.
If Open Source Scout executed full AI evaluations (evaluating codebase fit, implementation complexity, PR risk, and customized setup steps) for all 50 issues on discovery:
- **Rate Limit Exhaustion:** Free / Tier-1 API tiers (Gemini 1.5, OpenAI, Groq) enforce strict quotas:
  - Gemini Free: **15 RPM (Requests Per Minute)** and **1,500 RPD (Requests Per Day)**.
  - Discovering 50 issues in one click would require 50 LLM calls, instantly triggering `429 Too Many Requests` after 15 items!
- **Token Inefficiency & Financial Waste:** Evaluating 50 issues consumes ~100k - 250k input tokens, yet a developer will only ever inspect or claim 1 to 3 issues in a single session.

---

## 2. Multi-Tier Evaluation Architecture

To deliver deep AI intelligence without exceeding RPM/RPD limits or burning unnecessary tokens, Scout must follow a **3-Tier Progressive Funnel**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Tier 1: Deterministic Engine [0 Tokens / Zero AI Cost / <5ms]
        A[50 Raw Issues from GitHub] --> B[Relevance Scorer 100-pt Formula]
        B --> C[Rank Top 10 by Skills & Preferences]
    end

    subgraph Tier 2: Speculative Micro-Eval [Optional / Batched / Max 3 RPM]
        C --> D{Score >= 75%?}
        D -->|Top 3 Candidates| E[Micro-Eval: 1 LLM Prompt for 3 issues]
        E --> F[Cache in Supabase / LocalStorage 24h TTL]
    end

    subgraph Tier 3: Deep AI Agentic Evaluation [On-Demand Only]
        C -->|User clicks Claim or Deep Dive| G[Token Bucket Limiter: Max 5 RPM]
        G --> H[Full Scout AI Architecture & Implementation Plan]
        H --> I[Store Evaluation in Database]
    end
```

### Architectural Components:

### 1. Tier 1: Deterministic Heuristic Scorer (Active Today, Zero AI Quota)
- Runs completely in-browser / edge in under 5ms.
- 100-point breakdown:
  - Language match: **35 pts**
  - Framework / Skill match: **25 pts**
  - Recency: **15 pts**
  - Competition (comments / stars): **15 pts**
  - Difficulty tags: **10 pts**
- **No LLM calls required.**

### 2. Tier 2: Batched Speculative Micro-Evaluation
- Instead of 50 individual calls, pass the top 3 issues in a **single batched prompt**:
  ```json
  {
    "issues": [
      { "id": 1, "title": "...", "body_snippet": "..." },
      { "id": 2, "title": "...", "body_snippet": "..." },
      { "id": 3, "title": "...", "body_snippet": "..." }
    ]
  }
  ```
- Requests 1 concise JSON response containing fit rating, difficulty enum, and key caveats.
- Consumes **1 single request** (preserving RPM limits).

### 3. Tier 3: Token Bucket Rate Limiter for On-Demand Deep Evaluation
- Implemented as an in-memory & persisted token bucket limiter:
  ```typescript
  // packages/scout-core/src/rateLimiter.ts
  export class AIRateLimiter {
    private tokens: number = 10; // max burst
    private lastRefill: number = Date.now();
    private readonly refillRatePerMin: number = 10; // 10 RPM max
    private dailyUsage: number = 0;
    private readonly maxDailyQuota: number = 500; // 500 RPD
    
    async acquire(): Promise<boolean> { ... }
  }
  ```
- When quota is near exhaustion, queue requests with visual progress: *"AI rate limit safety active: 2 requests queued, processing in 12s..."*.

---

## 3. Deliverables & Next Steps
- [ ] Create `AIRateLimiter` utility to protect Gemini/OpenAI endpoints against RPM and RPD spikes.
- [ ] Implement response caching in Supabase (`ai_evaluations` table) keyed by `issue_url` with 48h TTL.
- [ ] Implement single-request Batched Micro-Eval for top 3 discovered issues.

issue.title: [Bug] Discovery surfaces already-claimed issues due to 'sort:updated-desc' and missing comment filters (<5% Maintainer Assignment Chance)
issue.body:
## 1. Problem Description & Root Cause Analysis

### The Flaw
In the Discovery dashboard, users are frequently presented with issues that have already been claimed by other contributors. 
For example, in `cashubtc/nutshell#620` (labeled `help wanted`), contributor `bavarianway` commented 8 hours prior stating:
> *"Hi! I'd like to pick this up, starting with LND-REST: Pydantic models for the status, invoice and payment responses..."*

When a user discovers this issue and comments *"Hi! I'd love to work on this issue..."*, the probability of maintainer assignment drops to **< 5%** because open-source maintainers almost universally assign issues on a **first-claimed, first-served** basis.

### Root Cause in Codebase
1. **GitHub API Query Inversion (`queryBuilder.ts`):**
   ```typescript
   // apps/web/src/utils/queryBuilder.ts
   // Current query structure:
   `is:open is:issue label:"${label}" language:${lang} sort:updated-desc`
   ```
   By sorting with `sort:updated-desc`, GitHub actively prioritizes issues with **recent activity**. When another developer comments *"I want to work on this"*, GitHub updates the issue's `updated_at` timestamp, **catapulting claimed/contested issues to the top of Scout's discovery results!**

2. **Absence of Push-Down Comment Constraints:**
   - The GitHub search API supports qualifiers such as `comments:0` (uncontested) or `comments:<=1`.
   - The query currently specifies no comment ceiling, nor does it push down `no:assignee` explicitly into the query string.

3. **Missing Intent Classification on Issue Timeline:**
   - There is no heuristic or regex scanner on recent issue comments to detect claim keywords (e.g., `"pick this up"`, `"take this"`, `"working on this"`, `"assign to me"`, `"PR incoming"`).

---

## 2. Architectural Solution & Proposed Implementation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Discovery Query Engine] --> B{Contestation Filter Mode}
    B -->|Strict: Uncontested| C[Query: comments:0 no:assignee]
    B -->|Balanced: Low-Competition| D[Query: comments:<=2 no:assignee]
    C --> E[GitHub Search API]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Comment Heuristic Scanner]
    F --> G{Claim Intent Detected?}
    G -->|Yes: Someone claimed in comments| H[Drop / Filter Out from Discovery]
    G -->|No: Discussion only| I[Calculate Contestation Risk Score]
    I --> J[Present in Discovery with High Success Rate]
```

### Step-by-Step Action Plan:
1. **Push-Down GitHub Qualifiers (`queryBuilder.ts`):**
   - Add `no:assignee` directly to the search query.
   - Introduce a configurable comment filter option in Discovery settings:
     - **Fresh Only (Default):** `comments:0` (guarantees 100% uncontested issues).
     - **Low Competition:** `comments:<=2` (filters out heated threads).
2. **Comment Intent Classifier (`apps/web/src/utils/claimDetector.ts`):**
   - For issues returned with `comments > 0`, inspect comment bodies using a regex intent filter:
     ```typescript
     const CLAIM_REGEX = /\b(i('d| would)? like to (work on|pick up|take)|assign (this to me|me)|working on a (pr|fix)|can i work on this)\b/i;
     ```
   - If a non-maintainer comment matches `CLAIM_REGEX`, mark the issue as `contested: true` and exclude it from the top Discovery stream.
3. **UI Contestation Indicator:**
   - Add a badge on `IssueCard.tsx`: `🟢 Fresh (0 comments)` or `🟡 1 comment (Discussion)`.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `queryBuilder.ts` adds `no:assignee` and configurable `comments:0` or `comments:<=1` push-down qualifiers.
- [ ] Issues with verbal claims in comments are automatically dropped or flagged as contested.
- [ ] Users no longer waste effort requesting assignment on issues where another contributor already claimed it first.

- Determine whether human prompts, cwd, timestamps, todos, compaction summaries, and archive state are recoverable.
- Check whether parsing needs anything beyond the Python standard library.
- If viable, implement it following `.agents/skills/add-harness/SKILL.md` with a synthetic fixture; otherwise record the findings in `docs/compatibility.md` under planned harnesses.

Do not commit real session data.
